Synopsis:
BOJ is set to hike rates 25bps to 1.25% at its Sept 17-18 meeting — the highest level in 31 years. Sources signal no preset terminal rate, with the board split between hawks and doves. Ueda expected to stay non-committal on pace but may echo July's message that hikes could accelerate if conditions warrant. Inflation pressures from a weak yen legacy and crude above $100/bbl keep the BOJ on guard, with analysts projecting rates reaching 1.75% by Q2 2027.
